$comment: The workflow examples, grouped as the docs present them. Every workflow is implemented in every language (unless 'unsupported' says otherwise) in that language's folder, and prints 'OK: <id>' when it succeeds. 'requires' names anything beyond a pool a workflow needs to do something real, and 'caution' what it changes that you may not want changed: try those on a test pool. A workflow with 'unsupported' is not implemented in the languages it names, each with the reason. The pages under docs/workflows/ are generated from this file, the sources and a run of every workflow.

workflows.title: Connect & inventory
workflows.description: Log in to a pool and take stock of it: read the pool name, enumerate the hosts and list the virtual machines with their power state. This is the starting point for every session.

workflows.title: Look up an object by UUID
workflows.description: Resolve a stable UUID back to a live object reference — how to persist a reference to an object across sessions.

workflows.title: Drive an asynchronous task
workflows.description: Start a long-running operation asynchronously to get a task back immediately, then poll it to completion and read its result — how to drive operations without blocking.

workflows.title: Handle an API error
workflows.description: Catch an API failure and inspect its error code and parameters — the shape of every error the API returns, and how to react to it robustly.

workflows.title: Trace API calls
workflows.description: Send a W3C trace context with your API calls, so the work the pool does for them is recorded as part of your application's distributed trace.

unsupported.java: The Java SDK cannot add an HTTP header to the requests it sends.

workflows.title: Event monitoring
workflows.description: Subscribe to the event stream and observe a change land as an event — the mechanism for keeping a client's view of the pool live.

workflows.title: Create a VM from a template
workflows.description: Clone one of the built-in templates and provision the clone into a real, installable VM.

workflows.title: Create a VM (full workflow)
workflows.description: Create a VM end to end: pick a template, name the VM, choose an installation source and a home server, set CPU & memory, add a disk on a storage repository, attach a network interface and start it — the full sequence, rather than a single clone call.

workflows.title: Clone a VM
workflows.description: Make a fast copy-on-write clone of a VM on the same storage repository — distinct from a full copy — the quick way to stamp out new VMs from a halted "golden" image.

workflows.title: Copy a VM
workflows.description: Make a full, independent copy of a VM onto a chosen storage repository (a deep copy of its disks) — distinct from a fast, copy-on-write clone.

workflows.title: Cross-pool copy a VM
workflows.description: Copy a VM from one pool to another: open a session to each pool, obtain a receiver token on the destination, then send a copy of the VM from the source. Takes the destination pool's URL as an extra argument after the password.

workflows.title: Delete a VM
workflows.description: Remove a VM and its owned disks: deleting a VM leaves its disks behind, so the disks are destroyed explicitly afterward.

workflows.title: Manage VM groups
workflows.description: Create an anti-affinity VM group, put a VM in it, read the membership back from the group side, then take the VM out again and delete the group.

workflows.title: Snapshot schedule
workflows.description: Create a scheduled-snapshot policy, attach a VM to it, run it on demand (the xe CLI version only creates and removes the schedule) and watch the retention limit prune the oldest snapshot away.

workflows.title: Manage VM disks
workflows.description: Deactivate a running VM's disk, resize it, reactivate it — the Activate/Deactivate and Resize operations from the VM's Storage tab.

workflows.title: VM power lifecycle
workflows.description: Drive a VM through its power states — start it, suspend it to memory, resume it and shut it down cleanly. Suspend and clean shutdown need the guest's cooperation, so this works on a throwaway copy of a VM with a guest OS and PV drivers (source_vm), which is deleted again with its disks afterwards.

workflows.title: Snapshot & revert
workflows.description: Take a snapshot of a VM and then revert the VM back to that point-in-time, as you would before a risky change.

workflows.title: Checkpoint & revert
workflows.description: Take a checkpoint of a running VM (disk AND memory, unlike a plain snapshot) and revert to it, as you would before a risky in-guest change. A checkpoint needs the guest's cooperation, so this works on a throwaway copy of a VM with a guest OS and PV drivers (source_vm).

workflows.title: Convert a VM to a template
workflows.description: Turn a VM into a reusable custom template. This is a one-way operation.

workflows.title: Edit VM properties
workflows.description: Change a VM's description and custom metadata, then read the changes back.

workflows.title: VM boot configuration
workflows.description: Set a VM's vCPU counts and boot order, then read them back.

workflows.title: Rename an object
workflows.description: Change an object's name and read it back — how any object is renamed.

workflows.title: Create a VM with a vGPU
workflows.description: Provision a VM from a template and assign it a virtual GPU: find a GPU group that offers a vGPU type, attach it, and read the assignment back.
workflows.requires: a GPU that supports vGPU, and a license that includes GPU virtualization (Premium Edition)

workflows.title: Get a VM's IP address
workflows.description: Read a running VM's IP address from its guest metrics, as reported by the in-guest agent.

workflows.title: List templates
workflows.description: Enumerate the pool's VM templates, both built-in and custom.

workflows.title: Manage a virtual TPM
workflows.description: Attach a virtual TPM to a halted VM, read it back and remove it again. A VM may have at most one, and only while it is halted.

workflows.title: Export and import a VM
workflows.description: Export a VM to an XVA file and import it back as a new one. These are HTTP transfers alongside the API rather than API calls, so the session id travels in the query string.

workflows.title: Configure dynamic memory
workflows.description: Give a VM a dynamic memory range so the host can reclaim memory from it under pressure, and see the ordering rule the four bounds must obey enforced.

workflows.title: Manage a VM's CD drive
workflows.description: Add a DVD drive to a VM, insert an ISO from the library and eject it again.

workflows.title: Create a VM and a template from a snapshot
workflows.description: Turn a snapshot into a new VM that stands on its own, and into a reusable custom template.

workflows.title: Manage a vApp
workflows.description: Group VMs into an appliance that starts and stops together in a defined order, start and shut it down as a unit, then remove it.

workflows.title: Attach a USB device to a VM
workflows.description: List the USB devices a host exposes, enable passthrough on one, attach it to a VM and detach it again.
workflows.requires: a USB device plugged into a host, and a license that includes USB pass-through (Premium Edition)
workflows.caution: a VM with a USB passed through cannot be snapshotted, suspended, or pool/storage migrated

workflows.title: Live migrate a VM
workflows.description: Move a running VM to another host in the pool with no downtime: check the destination can boot it, live-migrate it and confirm where it now runs. Uses a throwaway copy of a VM with a guest OS and PV drivers (source_vm), with its disks moved first to a shared storage repository (sr_name) so the destination host can see them.

workflows.title: Storage live-migration
workflows.description: Move a running VM's virtual disk to a different storage repository while the VM keeps running — live storage migration. Uses a throwaway copy of a VM with a guest OS and PV drivers (source_vm).

workflows.title: Create an NFS SR
workflows.description: Create a shared NFS storage repository on an NFS export (nfs_server, nfs_path), then detach and forget it.

workflows.title: Create an iSCSI SR
workflows.description: Connect a storage repository to a LUN on an iSCSI target, discovering the target's IQNs and then the LUNs behind one, as the New SR wizard does. Creating the SR formats the LUN, and a shared array offers many targets, so name yours with target_iqn.
workflows.caution: formats the LUN it uses (name it with scsi_id; it refuses a LUN that already holds an SR) and destroys the new SR again afterwards

workflows.title: Create an SMB SR
workflows.description: Connect a shared storage repository to an SMB/CIFS file share, passing the server, share path and credentials (the password as a secret, never in plain text).

workflows.title: Create an HBA SR
workflows.description: Connect a shared storage repository to a fibre-channel (HBA) LUN: discover the LUNs the host can see with a deliberately failing probe, then create the SR by SCSI ID. Creating the SR formats the LUN.
workflows.requires: a Fibre Channel or SAS LUN
workflows.caution: formats the LUN it uses (name it with scsi_id; it refuses a LUN that already holds an SR) and destroys the new SR again afterwards

workflows.title: Create an ISO library SR
workflows.description: Connect an ISO-library storage repository to a file share of ISO images (here an NFS export), so the images are available as installation media.

workflows.title: Attach a new disk
workflows.description: Create a fresh virtual disk on a storage repository and attach it to a VM.

workflows.title: Inventory a VM's disks
workflows.description: List a VM's attached disks and the size of each.

workflows.title: Storage repository usage
workflows.description: Report each storage repository's used and total capacity, and rescan one.

workflows.title: Reclaim freed space on a thin SR
workflows.description: Reclaim space freed by deleted disks on a thin-provisioned storage repository: find a trim-capable SR, pick a host with a live connection to it, and run the trim operation.

workflows.title: Detach, reattach and forget storage
workflows.description: Take a storage repository offline and bring it back: disconnect it from every host, reconnect and rescan it, then disconnect it once more and forget it for good.

workflows.title: Point an SR at moved storage
workflows.description: When the storage behind an SR moves to a new address, point the SR at it: a host's connection to an SR cannot be edited, so unplug each one, recreate it with the new settings and plug it back.

workflows.title: Copy a disk's contents
workflows.description: Upload data into a virtual disk, download the disk's raw contents and copy them into a second disk, then check that the copy matches. Disk contents travel as HTTP transfers alongside the API.

workflows.title: Set the pool's default storage
workflows.description: Choose where the pool puts new disks, suspended VMs' memory images and host crash dumps by default, then put the original choice back.

workflows.title: Attach an existing disk to another VM
workflows.description: Move a disk between VMs by detaching and re-attaching it, without copying the data.

workflows.title: Back up with changed block tracking
workflows.description: Walk an incremental backup: turn on changed block tracking, snapshot twice, ask the server which blocks differ, then release the older snapshot's data while keeping the change metadata the next incremental needs.

workflows.title: Create a network
workflows.description: Create an internal network — an isolated virtual switch with no physical NIC — for VMs to talk to each other privately.

workflows.title: List networks
workflows.description: Enumerate the pool's networks with their physical and virtual interface counts.

workflows.title: Manage network interfaces
workflows.description: Attach a virtual network interface to a VM and remove it again.

workflows.title: Create a NIC bond
workflows.description: Bond two spare network interfaces onto a new network for redundancy and throughput, read the bond back, then dissolve it.
workflows.requires: two spare network interfaces on one host

workflows.title: Host information
workflows.description: Read a host's software version, edition and CPU topology (sockets and cores).

workflows.title: Enter & exit maintenance mode
workflows.description: Put a host into maintenance mode: disable it so it accepts no new VMs, evacuate its running guests to another host in the pool, then re-enable it. A throwaway copy of a VM with a guest OS and PV drivers (source_vm), with its disks on a shared storage repository (sr_name), gives evacuation something to move.
workflows.caution: moves the host's running VMs to other hosts while it is in maintenance mode

workflows.title: Read host & VM metrics
workflows.description: Read live host metrics (total/free memory, liveness) and VM metrics (vCPU count, memory).

workflows.title: Read RRD performance metrics
workflows.description: Pull recent host performance samples from the RRD archives over the performance-data HTTP API, parse the legends and data, and summarise a metric (here the peak PVS Accelerator cache-space utilisation per host).

workflows.title: Pool properties
workflows.description: Read the pool name and default storage repository, then rename the pool and restore it.

workflows.title: Configure high availability
workflows.description: Turn on pool High Availability: choose a shared SR as the heartbeat statefile, compute how many host failures the pool can tolerate, enable HA, then disable it again.
workflows.caution: while HA is on, it can restart hosts it considers failed

workflows.title: Raise and dismiss alerts
workflows.description: List the pool's alerts, then dismiss one — what the Notifications view does.

workflows.title: Configure host power on
workflows.description: Set a host's out-of-band power-on mode and credentials, then read them back.
workflows.requires: a power-on method configured on the hosts (IPMI, Wake-on-LAN or a custom script)

workflows.title: Rotate the pool secret
workflows.description: Rotate the shared secret that authenticates pool members to each other.

workflows.title: Manage TLS certificates
workflows.description: Install a pool-wide CA certificate, reset a host's server certificate, read the resulting fingerprints back, and turn on verification of the certificates members present to each other.

workflows.title: Change the root password
workflows.description: Change the local superuser password to a temporary one and back again, noting that a root session's old password is not checked.
workflows.caution: changes the root password; a failure part way can lock you out of the host

workflows.title: GPU inventory
workflows.description: Enumerate the pool's GPU groups, their physical GPUs and the vGPU types each offers.

workflows.title: PVS Accelerator inventory
workflows.description: Document a pool's Citrix Provisioning (PVS) Accelerator setup: each site's read cache (host, size, storage), its PVS servers (addresses and streaming port range), and which VMs are accelerated versus the whole pool.

workflows.title: Configure PVS Accelerator
workflows.description: Build a PVS Accelerator site from nothing and take it down again: introduce the site and a PVS server, put a read cache on each host's local storage, accelerate a VM by proxying its first NIC, then remove the proxy and the server and forget the site, which removes its cache storage.

workflows.title: Configure NRPE monitoring
workflows.description: Configure a host's NRPE (Nagios Remote Plugin Executor) agent through the monitoring plugin: read its status and configuration, enable it and permit a monitoring host, then read it back.

workflows.title: Configure SNMP monitoring
workflows.description: Configure a host's SNMP agent through the monitoring plugin: read its configuration, enable it with a community string, then read the configuration and running status back.

workflows.title: Manage SSH access
workflows.description: Open the pool's SSH service with an automatic cut-off, read back when it lapses, then close it again — the pool-level call fans out to every host.

workflows.title: Change control domain memory
workflows.description: Read and change a host's control domain (dom0) memory, then put it back. One setter pins the static and dynamic bounds together, because dom0 does not balloon.

workflows.title: Back up a host's configuration
workflows.description: Download a host's configuration backup and hand it back as a restore would — and watch another host's backup be refused.

workflows.title: Collect a server status report
workflows.description: Gather a host's diagnostic bundle: read the catalogue of sections it can report on, download the whole bundle, then download a smaller one covering only the sections you pick.

workflows.title: Restart a host
workflows.description: Take a host down and bring it back: stop it accepting new VMs, move the ones it is running elsewhere, reboot it, then power it right off and back on again.

workflows.title: Clear a host's crash dumps
workflows.description: Find the crash dumps a host kept after a failure, report how big and how old they are, then delete them to free the space.

workflows.title: Configure pool options
workflows.description: Read and change the pool-wide options that govern how it behaves — live patching, IGMP snooping and memory-migration compression — then put them back.

workflows.title: Configure console access
workflows.description: Tighten how consoles and management traffic may be used: idle timeouts for the pool's own consoles and for VM consoles, one session at a time, and refusing plain HTTP.

workflows.title: Configure host storage
workflows.description: Set a host's iSCSI initiator name and turn on storage multipathing, then restore both.

workflows.title: Send logs to a remote syslog server
workflows.description: Point a host's logs at a remote syslog server — and reconfigure the daemon, without which the setting is recorded but nothing changes.

workflows.title: Manage device driver variants
workflows.description: Inspect a host's device drivers and choose which variant of one to use, seeing the difference between the variant that is selected and the one currently loaded.

workflows.title: Manage pool membership
workflows.description: List the pool's member hosts and which one coordinates it, promote a different host to coordinator, then promote the original back.
workflows.caution: hands the coordinator role to another host and back, which restarts the toolstack on every host and briefly drops every management connection

workflows.title: Configure clustering
workflows.description: Enable the clustering layer that shared block storage needs for thin provisioning, then watch quorum as a host leaves the cluster and rejoins it.
workflows.requires: shared block storage for a GFS2 cluster

workflows.title: Read workload-balancing recommendations
workflows.description: Point the pool at a workload-balancing appliance, read its placement recommendations for the pool and for one VM, then disconnect it.

workflows.title: Configure updates (CDN)
workflows.description: Point the pool at a CDN update repository and turn on automatic update sync: register a repository, set it as the pool's repository, enable update sync, read it back, then tidy up.

workflows.title: Configure updates for an air-gapped pool
workflows.description: Switch a pool with no internet access to offline updates: make an update bundle repository the pool's only repository, upload an update bundle (.xsbundle) to it if you have one, list the updates it makes available, then tidy up.

workflows.title: Apply updates from the CDN
workflows.description: Sync the pool's update metadata from the CDN and apply it to every host, then read each host's post-update reboot guidance.
workflows.requires: High Availability and Workload Balancing turned off first, as the update documentation describes (turn them back on afterwards)

workflows.title: Rolling pool update
workflows.description: Apply the CDN's updates across the pool host by host, coordinator first: sync the metadata, then for each host apply the updates, moving its VMs to the rest of the pool and rebooting it only when the update requires, so the VMs keep running.
workflows.requires: High Availability and Workload Balancing turned off first, as the update documentation describes (turn them back on afterwards)
workflows.caution: updates every host, one at a time, moving its VMs off and rebooting it when the update requires

workflows.title: Tag and organize objects
workflows.description: Organize a pool with tags and folders: add tags to a VM and a host (tags work on any object type), place the VM in a folder, read it all back, then tidy up.

workflows.title: Tag the pool
workflows.description: Add and remove a tag on the pool itself, showing that tags apply to the pool, not just VMs and hosts.

workflows.title: Custom fields
workflows.description: Attach and read custom name/value fields on a VM — arbitrary metadata you define, stored on the object.

workflows.title: Manage Active Directory users
workflows.description: Join the pool to an Active Directory domain, grant an AD user access with an RBAC role, read it back, then tidy up.

workflows.title: List RBAC roles
workflows.description: Enumerate the pool's role-based access control (RBAC) roles — the roles that can be granted to users.

workflows.title: Manage Secure Boot certificates
workflows.description: Check whether the pool can supply UEFI Secure Boot certificates and whether a guest is ready to use them, then flag a guest whose certificates have gone stale for a refresh at its next boot — and unflag it again.
workflows.caution: updating a guest's certificates can trigger BitLocker recovery (TPM PCR7 changes)

workflows.title: Configure disaster recovery
workflows.description: Replicate the pool's metadata (the configuration of its VMs and vApps) to an iSCSI or Fibre Channel SR, so that a pool at a disaster recovery site can recover the VMs from the storage array's replica of that SR.
workflows.requires: an iSCSI or Fibre Channel SR attached to every host

workflows.title: Fail over to a disaster recovery site
workflows.description: On the pool at the disaster recovery site, attach the storage array's replica of the protected pool's storage, read the pool metadata replicated to it, and recover the VMs and vApps it describes. By default it is a test failover, which removes what it recovered and detaches the replica again.
workflows.requires: a pool at the disaster recovery site, and the storage array's replica of the protected pool's iSCSI or Fibre Channel SR (target, IQN and SCSI id), with the mirror broken
workflows.caution: never attach a LUN that another pool still has attached: two pools using one LUN corrupt it
